source_fields.formulation: The current scalar quadratic loss depends on a window of recent actions, and the learner observes only its value on that window. The comparator uses the same fixed action throughout every window. The complete loss sequence is fixed before interaction.
source_fields.solution_goal: Minimize performance as defined by the metric, guarantee, and native resource.

source_fields.instance: Each action is $x_t\in[0,1]$, with fixed initial history $x_{1-m:0}=0$. Memory length $m\ge2$ includes the current action; two previous actions plus the current action correspond to $m=3$. $$f_t:[0,1]^m\to\mathbb R\ \text{is convex quadratic},\qquad |f_t(z)|\le B,\qquad\|\nabla f_t(z)\|_2\le L\quad(\forall z\in[0,1]^m).$$ All $f_{1:T}$ are fixed before the learner's private randomness is generated; loss coefficients do not depend on realized past actions.

operations.query_signature: Choose $x_t$ using only past scalar feedback, then observe the realized memory loss $f_t(x_{t-m+1:t})$ without gradients. There is no additional measurement noise beyond environmental or algorithmic randomness. Causal randomized policies remain in $[0,1]$. Inputs $T,m,B,L$ and the initial history are public; quadratic coefficients are hidden. Past feedback may be stored and reused computationally; no additional historical or sample queries are available beyond the explicitly declared interface.

source_fields.feasibility: The output is the complete action trajectory satisfying feasibility and timing requirements. Randomized mixtures may be implemented before acting. Retrospective averages or convex combinations cannot replace actions that have already incurred loss. No additional optimal value or certificate is required.
source_fields.allowed_postprocessing: Previously executed online actions cannot be changed.
source_fields.certificate_requirement: No function value, optimality certificate, or final recommendation is required unless explicitly listed for this axis.

source_fields.normalization: Use the cumulative quantity over T rounds without dividing by T. Preserve the displayed order of probability or expectation.
source_fields.finiteness_conditions: Every actual or constant-comparator window loss has absolute value at most B, so memory-comparator loss differences lie in [-2BT,2BT].

components.description: $T$ sequential rounds, or $T$ rounds per task

The learner's actions before round $1$ are zero. The displayed constant-$u$ comparator also uses $u$ before round $1$. Forcing the comparator to share the zero prehistory changes only the first $m-1$ terms, and the benchmarks differ by at most $2B(m-1)$; retain this finite-horizon difference. There is one scalar observation per round, $N=T$. All initialization and exploration are charged, with distinct information, arithmetic, communication, and memory resources.

source_fields.scalarization: Compare only at the specified joint budget and with the same native performance measure.
source_fields.setup_cost: All initialization, exploration, and identification calls are included in the budget.
source_fields.precision_model: Exact real-arithmetic model; bit complexity is unspecified

source_fields.complete_expression: Take the infimum over causal algorithms and supremum over admissible loss rules, averaging over randomness. Fixed loss functions are replayed within constant-length windows; the comparator uses the explicitly stated history convention.
